events.verdict: Grimes (PHI) is in the paint for less than three seconds when he is imminently exiting.
Claxton (BKN) is in the lane for longer than three seconds.
Watford (BKN) straddles the lane line and is in the paint for longer than three seconds without imminently actively guarding an opponent.

Maxey (PHI) cleanly ties the ball up in Johnson's (BKN) hands as he jumps in the air to contest the driving shot attempt. The simultaneous arm contact that occurs with Johnson's left arm is incidental. With the block the ball becomes dislodged, so a play-on, rather than a whistled jump ball is appropriate.
Oubre Jr. (PHI) initiates contact with Claxton's (BKN) back, which affects the jump shot attempt.
Watford (BKN) initiates contact with Oubre Jr.'s (PHI) right arm, which affects his play at the basket.
Claxton (BKN) cleanly blocks the shot attempt prior to when the ball reaches its apex.
George (PHI) and Johnson (BKN) come together in pursuit of the loose ball and incidental foot to foot contact occurs that dislodges Johnson from his position.

Watford's (BKN) does not abnormally move his off-arm at the start of the drive and the contact that occurs with Oubre Jr.'s (PHI) face is incidental. Contact to an opponent's head/face can be deemed marginal when the result of a natural basketball move, provided the contact is not disproportionate or uncontrolled.
George (PHI) reaches for the loose ball and marginal contact occurs with Claxton's (BKN) right arm as he secures rebound and attempts the shot near the basket.
